title: TTI vs Chervon: The Lawsuit, the Rivalry and the Numbers
seoTitle: TTI vs Chervon: Lawsuit, Court History and Results
dek: TTI has sued Chervon and its new CEO, TTI's own former chief Joe Galli, over trade secrets and a wave of hires. WCB's file on the case, twenty years of litigation between the two groups, and how their businesses compare.
description: WCB's running file on TTI v. Chervon and Joe Galli (N.D. Ill. 1:26-cv-13942): the trade-secrets complaint, every earlier patent case between TTI, Milwaukee and Chervon since 2005, a timeline of Galli's move and hires, and five years of revenue for both companies.

status.label: Case filed 9 Nov 2026 · no response yet
status.text: As of 15 November the docket shows only the complaint and three routine filings. TTI has not moved for a preliminary injunction, and neither Chervon nor Galli has responded in public.

summary: On 9 November 2026, TTI North America, Milwaukee Tool and TTI's sales company R&B sued Chervon North America, Chervon Holdings and Joe Galli in federal court in Chicago. The complaint says Galli, TTI's chief executive from 2008 to 2024, kept a 'covert channel' to a serving TTI sales executive who passed him confidential sales and financial information, and that after Galli became Chervon's CEO in September the company hired at least 30 former TTI employees in seven weeks. TTI brings eight counts, led by trade-secret misappropriation. These are allegations; the court has not ruled.

It is not the first time the two groups have met in court. TTI won a preliminary injunction against a Chervon-made laser level in 2005, and Milwaukee sued Chervon over lithium-ion battery patents in 2014. Since 2019 the traffic has run the other way: Chervon sued TTI over EGO lawn-mower patents, and in February 2025 a Delaware jury found that TTI had wilfully infringed five of them.

Behind the lawsuits is a fight for the same customers. TTI is far larger, with 2025 revenue of USD 15.26 billion against Chervon's USD 1.63 billion, but the brands meet head to head: Milwaukee against FLEX for professionals, RYOBI against EGO and SKIL for homeowners, The Home Depot against Lowe's on the shelf. The people TTI says Chervon hired are the sales, recruiting and product managers who built Milwaukee's lead.

questions.q: What is TTI accusing Chervon and Galli of?
questions.a: Misappropriating trade secrets and inducing TTI employees to break their contracts. The complaint says Galli received confidential TTI sales and financial information from a serving sales executive between June 2025 and February 2026, and that Chervon hired at least 30 former TTI staff in seven weeks without any screen to keep TTI information out. These are allegations the court has not ruled on.

questions.q: Has Chervon beaten TTI in court before?
questions.a: Yes. In February 2025 a Delaware jury found that TTI wilfully infringed five Chervon lawn-mower patents and awarded just under USD 4 million as a reasonable royalty. Earlier, TTI won a preliminary injunction against a Chervon-made laser level in 2005, and Milwaukee sued Chervon over battery patents in 2014.

questions.q: Why can't TTI just enforce Galli's non-compete?
questions.a: Galli's two-year non-solicitation clause ran out around May 2026, before he joined Chervon. TTI says it is not suing on his agreements and instead relies on trade-secret law and on other employees' own covenants, many of which carry 12-month restrictions, some naming Chervon as a competitor.

Most trade-secret cases settle. The near-term signs to watch are whether TTI asks for a preliminary injunction, whether Chervon challenges the Illinois court's jurisdiction over Chervon Holdings and Galli, and whether Chervon makes a Hong Kong disclosure. WCB's analysis sets out four possible endings.

questions.q: Which is bigger, TTI or Chervon?
questions.a: TTI, by about nine times: USD 15.26 billion of revenue in 2025 against Chervon's USD 1.63 billion. Chervon grew faster in the first half of 2026, 12.8% against 5.9%, after a weak 2025.

facts.label: Filed
facts.value: 9 November 2026, US District Court for the Northern District of Illinois (Chicago), case 1:26-cv-13942, jury trial demanded

facts.label: Parties
facts.value: TTI North America, Milwaukee Electric Tool and R&B Sales & Marketing v. Chervon North America, Chervon Holdings and Joseph Galli Jr.

facts.label: Claims
facts.value: Eight counts: federal and Illinois trade-secret misappropriation, tortious interference with contract (three counts), unfair competition, aiding and abetting breach of fiduciary duty, unjust enrichment

facts.label: Core allegations
facts.value: From June 2025 to February 2026 a TTI sales SVP sent Galli store, sales and customer information and Milwaukee CFO slides; Chervon hired at least 30 former TTI staff between 10 Sep and 3 Nov 2026

facts.label: Relief sought
facts.value: Damages and lost profits, disgorgement, punitive damages, return of property, and injunctions on using TTI information and hiring TTI staff still under covenants; no amount stated

facts.label: Since filing
facts.value: Chervon's Hong Kong shares fell more than 9% intraday on 12 Nov. No injunction motion and no public response as of 15 Nov
